title: Rollout Acceptance Rubric + Cadence Dashboard
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet is a compact, phase-driven rollout acceptance rubric paired with a cadence dashboard view. It's designed for product-ops leads running staged feature activations where we want fast go/no-go decisions, clear signal ownership, and a compact KPI snapshot for each phase. Use this as the canonical quick-check during preflight and the first 72 hours of live traffic.

How to use (quick):
- Populate the phase row for your feature (alpha -> beta -> ramp -> general availability).
- Assign owners for each signal column and set thermostat thresholds (green/amber/red).
- During cadence checkpoints (daily for ramp, twice-daily for beta), update the metric cells and tick the acceptance box.
- If any red triggers, follow the Decision Tree section.

Phase definitions (this doc's lens):
- Alpha: internal test orgs, 0-1% traffic, safety-focused.
- Beta: invited external customers, ~1-10% traffic, KPIs monitored closely.
- Ramp: gradual scale 10-75%, capacity-focused, latency SLO stress.
- GA: >75% traffic, business SLAs enabled.

Acceptance rubric (per-phase rows you should copy into your feature line):
Columns: Acceptance (yes/no), Traffic target, Error rate (p95) threshold, End-to-end latency (p95), Cost per 1k tokens or units, Quality regression (eval set), Infrastructure headroom (% GPU alloc free), UX complaints (per 10k users), Feature flag health (toggle incidents)
additional_notes: Owners should maintain a short daily log line in the cadence dashboard cell (who updated, snapshot at 09:00/15:00). Keep links to experiment configs in the linked_artifacts list. This is intentionally compact—if you need deeper diagnostics, link to the troubleshooting playbook (confluence:PRODOPS-3601).
decision_tree:
Go/No-go decision tree (abbreviated):
- If Acceptance == yes and all thermostats green => proceed to next phase.
- If any amber thermostats + mitigations available => pause and apply mitigation, re-evaluate at next checkpoint.
- If any red thermostats => rollback or immediate mitigation per SRE runbook. Notify exec on-call if GA target.

Thermostat examples (practical thresholds):
- Error rate (server errors): green <0.1%, amber 0.1-0.5%, red >0.5%
- Latency (p95): green <300ms, amber 300-600ms, red >600ms
- Cost/unit: green within forecast +10%, amber +10-25%, red >+25%

KPI list (for the dashboard columns):
- Leading: request rate (rps), queuing depth, KV cache hit %, prefix reuse %, early aborts
- Lagging: p95 latency, p99 latency, 5xx rate, SLO burn rate, infra CPU/GPU utilization
- Business: DAU impact, retention delta (7d), refunds/credits, NPS feedback counts

Owners & responsibilities (short):
- Product-ops: cadence facilitation, gating decision, stakeholder broadcast
- Eng on-call: mitigate infra/perf, apply temporary throttles
- Model/ML owner: quality regression triage, prompt/param rollbacks
- Solutions/CS: customer outreach, triage incoming complaints

Pre-launch checklist (compact):
- [ ] Canary traffic config + kill-switch validated
- [ ] Automated smoke test runbook + green
- [ ] Load profile sims completed for ramp target
- [ ] Backfill eval set for core prompts + baseline outputs saved
- [ ] Cost model updated (1k-token baseline)
- [ ] Observability: traces, token-level billing, alerting rules in place

Example cadence schedule (recommended):
- Alpha: checkpoint once (end of day)
- Beta (days 0–3): checkpoints 09:00 and 17:00 local; escalate on red
- Ramp (0–7): morning metrics + mid-day smoke; if stable, daily checks then every-other-day
- GA: daily for 3 days then weekly

Quick triage playbook (if red):
1) Identify which column(s) hit red (infra/quality/cost/UX).
2) If infra -> throttle traffic, increase pool, fallback to cheaper model variant.
3) If quality -> switch model pin, reduce generation params, notify ML owner.
4) If cost -> enable strict batching/caching profile or reduce max tokens.
5) If UX -> enable partial rollout or rollback and notify CS.

Open questions / known TODOs (notes to self):
- Add a compact heatmap export that PMs can embed in stakeholder slides (ask growth-design).
- Consolidate thermostat thresholds with SRE to align with on-call playbooks.
- Decide canonical place for small-features GA signoff vs larger feature releases.

Slack shortlinks to use while running: #prodops-cadence, #sre-oncall, #model-quality.

Revision history (brief):
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Evelyn)
- 2025-12-02: added thermostat thresholds and triage playbook (Miguel)
- 2026-02-10: clarified cadence schedule and ownership (Priya)

If you're running a rollout this week, copy this sheet into a per-feature file and ping the prodops rotation to claim the gating slot.
